title: Latvia Gets a New Leader After Drones Cause a Government Shake-Up
summary: What would you do if a drone from a war zone accidentally flew into your country? That’s exactly what happened in Latvia, a small country in Europe near Russia. Several drones, probably from Ukraine, crossed into Latvia’s airspace. They didn’t cause much damage, but they scared a lot of people. The government argued about how to handle it, and the prime minister, Evika Silina, had to resign. On Thursday, Latvia’s parliament voted in a new prime minister: Andris Kulbergs. He’s 47 and leads a new four-party coalition. Kulbergs said his top job is to keep Latvia safe—not just from military threats, but also to protect the economy and energy supplies. Latvia used to be part of the Soviet Union, but now it’s in NATO and the European Union. That means it’s on the same team as the U.S. and many other countries. The new government says it will stay pro-Western and keep supporting Ukraine in its war against Russia. The drone incidents are a reminder that the war isn’t far away. Russian and Ukrainian drones have crashed in Latvia and its neighbors before. Kulbergs’ government has a strong majority in parliament, so it should be able to pass laws easily. Elections are coming in October, so the new team has just a few months to show it can handle the job.
why_it_matters: This shows how events in one country can affect neighbors, and how countries must work together to stay safe and protect their people.

background_read: Latvia is a small country in Northern Europe, with about 1.9 million people.
After being part of the Soviet Union until 1991, it joined NATO and the European Union to stay safe and connected.
Recently, drones from the war in Ukraine have sometimes crossed into Latvia and other nearby countries, causing alarm.
Article_Structure: WHO: Andris Kulbergs, the new prime minister; former PM Evika Silina; Latvia’s parliament
WHAT: Latvia’s government changed after a drone incident led to the prime minister resigning; a new coalition government with Kulbergs took over
WHY: Drones from Ukraine crossed the border, causing political debate; the new government promises safety, a pro-Western stance, and support for Ukraine

perspectives.description: The new government’s supporters say a fresh coalition can better handle security and keep Latvia strong within NATO and the EU.
Some people worry that frequent government changes might make it hard to make long-term plans and might show weakness to Russia.
Analysts note that many small countries with coalition governments experience quick changes when crises happen.
